title: Grateful Dead Live at Seminole Indian Village on 1969-05-24

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of an average‑to‑below‑average 1969 show – decent first jam and a solid Feedback, but uneven playing and a few technical hiccups.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that sounds okay overall but suffers from a noticeable cut, a pitch wobble on a solo, and a thin drum mix. Musically the night has flashes of brilliance—the early jam (China Cat > The Eleven) and a surprisingly tight Feedback—yet many numbers drag or lose tempo, especially Alligator and the Drums segment. Fans who love rare ’69 material will find it worth hearing despite its unevenness.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is judged average to below‑average with a few highlights, while the soundboard recording is usable but not pristine; combined score lands in the mid‑range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall decent clarity but includes a 36‑second cut, a -2% pitch anomaly on a solo, and thin drum presence; occasional muddiness in the second set.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > The Eleven (early jam)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first half flows better with a strong jam, but the second set loses momentum as songs become uneven and the drum segment feels disjointed.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Enters a brief unique jam early on; otherwise his playing is unremarkable in this performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum mix sounds thin and lacks interplay, described as “shoes in the dryer” with no cohesion.
